runtime.note: sha256 of agent_os/build/model-runtime-production-probe/libtraceform_local_model.so, recorded in its experimental_model_build.json

change: GBNF grammar-constrained decoding added to the app's JNI wrapper (agent_os/android/native/experimental_local_model.cpp) over the pinned llama.cpp runtime d78f40d9d34d7a72ecdcd2e854f75ff86afc8ca3, opt-in per call via a grammar argument (grammar + greedy in one sampler chain).

grammar_json3.criterion: each case returned a JSON object that parsed and contained every key listed for that case (presence only; value types and content were not scored)
grammar_json3.note: the grammar forces key presence and key order, so this measures that decoding ran to completion within 128 new tokens, not answer quality

prompt_only_json2.criterion: same presence-only check, schema prompt, fence/think stripping, one retry
prompt_only_json2.failure_mode: 9 of 10 cases produced no JSON at all: the model spent the 128-token budget inside a <think> block before the object

paired_comparison.result: 10/10 with grammar vs 1/10 without, on MiniCPM5-2B
paired_comparison.interpretation: the gap is mostly budget allocation: the grammar prevents reasoning tokens from consuming the 128-token window, so it is not evidence of better reasoning

timing.note: per-case wall clock measured from before prepare() and including a full 1.56 GB model load on every call; one run; no repeats; no thermal or background-load control

not_comparable.d2_strict_json: 0/10 was Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_0 on ten different single-key prompts scored by exact string match on raw fenced output with no recovery; re-parsing those recorded outputs with StructuredOutput.parse yields 10/10, so the 0/10 reflects the old parse policy and a different model, not this comparison
not_comparable.earlier_prompt_only_9_of_10: that run used Qwen2.5-1.5B, not MiniCPM5-2B, so it must not be read as a baseline for the grammar number

limitations: the grammar enumerates the required keys in order and allows any value, so key presence is guaranteed by construction
the 'plan' case returned the prompt's own Example object verbatim
content is still wrong where it was wrong unconstrained: the 'schedule' case returned 2023 dates for 'tomorrow', 'summary' returned a placeholder sentence with tags [word,word]
per-key types are not enforced (the 'error' case returned a boolean although the prompt asked for a string); the grammar generator supports flat objects only
10/10 is one run of the fixed build; two earlier runs aborted the app with SIGABRT before the sampler-chain fix, and those runs are not counted here
timing includes per-case model load and prepare(); no repeats, variance, thermal or background-load control
the probe truncates each recorded output to 200 characters, which is enough to score keys but not enough to audit full content or truncation boundaries
the app's user-facing document flow still passes no grammar (LocalModelDraft.java passes null)
command: adb -s 25161JEGR06836 shell am start -n org.traceform.agentos.actionsvalidation/org.traceform.agentos.LocalModelQualityProbe -a JSON3|JSON2 --es model minicpm

budget_experiment.question: does the 1/10 prompt-only result come from the 128-token budget rather than from an inability to emit JSON?
budget_experiment.interpretation: raising the budget from 128 to 512 lifts the prompt-only arm from 1/10 to 5/10 while every failure at 128 was a think block that consumed the window; grammar removes the failure entirely at 128. The budget-allocation explanation is therefore supported, but prompt-only is still far from the grammar arm at 512.

content_scoring.criterion: per-case checks: JSON type of specific keys, ISO year for schedule, placeholder text, repeated tags, empty note, verbatim prompt example
failures: plan: steps repeat the prompt's example [pack, go] verbatim
error: error field is not a string although the prompt asked for a string
schedule: start and end are not in 2026 (the run date year)
summary: placeholder sentence and repeated tag word
content_scoring.interpretation: the grammar guarantees shape only; half the cases still fail content, so the 10/10 shape number must never be read as quality

timing_repeat.note: the same code and model produced a 32% higher median in the repeat run; treat single-run timing as indicative only

unseen_cases.criterion: top-level keys present; nested objects checked at the top level only
observations: nested objects work once the grammar defines a child rule
removing the schema prompt with its example did not change the result, so the example leak is not what makes these pass
copy-from-prompt worked: the token QX7 was reproduced in both arms
content quality still varies: the plain arm invented 'Alex' and 'monospace' while the schema arm used placeholders
unseen_cases.generator_finding: GBNF rule names must be alphabetic; a generated name like obj_867202238 made llama_sampler_init_grammar return null, which surfaced as 'grammar could not be applied'. Renaming to suba0 fixed it.
